title: Superposition of Light Waves from Point Sources
full_prompt: Create a high-performance wave interference visualization in ManimGL. Define a custom Mobject class named `LightWaveSlice` that inherits from `Mobject` and utilizes a custom ModernGL shader to compute and render the superposition of light waves from multiple point sources in real-time. The class should take a `DotCloud` representing the point sources and dynamically pass their coordinates as uniforms to the shader. Implement methods to update uniforms such as frequency, wave number, decay factor, and time. Create a scene named `SuperpositionOfPoints` where several point sources are initialized, animated to move, and the resulting dynamic interference patterns (including amplitude and intensity views) are displayed on a 2D slice.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Missing shader files or incorrect shader folder path
common_failure_modes.note: The custom shader folder 'diffraction_shader' must exist and contain valid vertex/fragment shaders compatible with ModernGL.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Performance lag due to CPU-bound wave calculations
common_failure_modes.note: Attempting to calculate wave superposition on the CPU for a dense grid instead of using GPU shaders will result in extremely low frame rates.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Uniform mismatch between Python and GLSL
common_failure_modes.note: The number of point sources in DotCloud must match the expected uniform array size or dynamic uniform names in the shader.
